newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire denies Kisangani city surrounded by rebels.
newsitem.headline: Zaire denies Kisangani city surrounded by rebels.

text.p: Zaire on Monday denied claims by rebels to have surrounded its third city of Kisangani, the base of its counter-offensive against a five-month guerrilla campaign.
"If they have surrounded Kisangani, where exactly are they?" a Defence Ministry spokesman asked.
"To the north and northeast they are around 100 km (60 miles) away. They may be within 50 km (30 miles) to the southeast," he added.
Tutsi-led rebels advancing in eastern Zaire said they had surrounded Kisangani, where civilians have been fleeing an expected attack.
The radio of the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) said the government was deserting Kisangani.
"The AFDL forces have now surrounded Kisangani," the Voice the People radio said from Goma, the largest city seized by rebels who now control a 1,000 km (600-mile) border strip.

"The people are awaiting the arrival of (rebel leader) Laurent Kabila. The AFDL forces are in evidence on the battle front in Kisangani and the Zairean government is fleeing," said the broadcast, monitored by the BBC.
No independent account of the situation around Kisangani was immediately available but travellers from the area said on Saturday there was no sign of rebels.
The government last reported fighting on Wednesday about 40 km (25 miles) to the north, the nearest it has placed the rebels to the city.
Several sources in Kisangani said the surrounding bush was heavily mined and the three main approach roads were manned by government troops and their mainly Serb mercenary backers.

The city straddles the Zaire River and would appear difficult to surround. Many civilians have left at night in dugout canoes, the safest way to escape without encountering either a minefield or government troops.
Rebels began targeting Kisangani after capturing Lubutu 200 km (120 miles) away and its nearby Tingi Tingi refugee camp.
The spokesman said Kisangani was calm, as was the international airport and military base 17 km (10 miles) to the northeast.
